programs.name: Veterans Exemption

tiers[0] (0-99, $1,000).quote: is exempted from taxation to the amount of one thousand dollars ($1,000), except in:

tiers[1] (100, $10,000).correct: 10000 ONLY where the city/town has adopted it by ordinance (local option, not a statutory baseline)
tiers[1] (100, $10,000).quote: may, by ordinance, passed in the city or town where the veteran's property is assessed ... receive a ten thousand dollar ($10,000) exemption from local taxation on his or her property

survivingSpouse.quote: or the property of the unmarried widow or widower of that person

wartimeRequired.quote: most veteran's conflict/metal qualifying events can be found under RI Gen Law 44-3-4.2 and 44-3-4.

localAmounts.correct: statute itself names dozens of town-specific amounts (e.g. Cumberland up to $47,544 and Cranston up to $250,000 for totally disabled; Westerly $39,000; North Kingstown $11,000); several towns use flat tax credits
localAmounts.quote: Cranston: up to $250,000, starting with the December 31, 2016 assessment

programs.effectiveChanges: 44-3-4 was last amended by P.L. 2025 ch. 189 and ch. 220 (eff. July 1, 2025) and again in May 2026 (H 7662, Middletown additional exemptions/credits), both town-specific insertions; the $1,000 base and $10,000 local-option tiers are unchanged for TY2026. Assessment date Dec 31, 2026 governs the 2027 bills.
programs.note: Two corrections to the modeling note: (1) the $10,000 totally-disabled tier under 44-3-4(c) exists only 'by ordinance' of the city or town, so it is a local option, not a statewide floor; the only guaranteed statewide figure is the $1,000 wartime exemption; (2) the DMF report (self-reported, Dec 31, 2021 assessment, released Sept 2022) shows the totally-disabled benefit ranging from a $90 credit to $250,000 of assessed value across municipalities, so the file's 'median $10,000' and '36 municipalities' could not be verified from it (the report covers all 39). Remarriage ends the widow/widower benefit unless the remarriage was void, ended by death, or was annulled/dissolved (subsection (d)).

programs.name: Gold Star Parents
programs.note: RIGL 44-3-5 was not opened for this pass; the row only cites the section. It is a parent-of-deceased-servicemember benefit and should never be credited to a rated veteran's own home.

missingPrograms.name: Specially adapted housing exemption (RIGL 44-3-4(b))
missingPrograms.what: A $10,000 exemption (towns may set more: Cranston up to $30,000, Narragansett up to $50,000, Westerly up to $40,500) for totally disabled veterans, or their unmarried widow/widower, who received VA specially adapted housing assistance and occupy the home as their domicile. The file's note calls this a 'full exemption'; the statute gives $10,000 (DMF report shows some towns self-report 100%).

jurisdictionNote.correct: RIGL 44-3-4: a $1,000 statewide exemption for wartime veterans and their unmarried widows/widowers; everything above that is set town by town. The $10,000 totally-disabled (100% service-connected) exemption and the $10,000 specially-adapted-housing exemption apply only where the city or town has adopted them by ordinance, and the statute itself lists dozens of town-specific amounts (from flat credits of a few hundred dollars to $250,000 of assessed value in Cranston). Modeled at the statutory figures; check the RI Division of Municipal Finance Veterans/Senior Exemptions Report (self-reported, 12/31/21 assessment) or your assessor for your town's amount.

summary: Rhode Island's only statewide floor is the $1,000 wartime exemption (surviving spouses included, so survivingSpouse must be true); the $10,000 totally-disabled tier and the $10,000 specially-adapted-housing exemption are local options adopted by ordinance, not baselines, and the file's 'full exemption for SAH' and 'median $10,000 across 36 municipalities' claims could not be verified. Effective rate 1.21% vs 1.12% is within tolerance; the DMF town-by-town report is still the Sept 2022 edition.
